open_questions: Status line: no plugin component, manifest key or mod API for a status line is documented. Can a plugin supply statusLine at all, and on which surfaces does a custom status line render (desktop, VS Code, cloud)?
Cloud sessions: do plugins synced from the user's claude.ai account (not declared in the repo) load in a cloud session? The docs say skills enabled on claude.ai load, but say nothing about plugins.

Cloud sessions: the mods overview says hooks run in a cloud session 'for a plugin that reaches the cloud session', but does not say which plugins reach it. If a repo ships a plugin directory of its own, does it load on web?

Desktop app: do plugin slash commands, plugin output styles and a status line work? The desktop page names skills, agents, hooks, MCP and LSP only. Do toasts and status-line-style mod output render there?
VS Code: which plugin commands appear in the 'Subset' slash menu? Do plugin MCP servers load? The AbovePrompt band is absent from the VS Code render-site table, so the band may not draw there.

Cowork: mods are documented as Claude Code only, but do Cowork's hooks and agents get a shell tool, and can Cowork read and write working-folder files? Cowork's status line and UI surfaces are not documented.

Programmatic API names in the request that the docs did not confirm: the 'claude-code' module name (the docs use hooks/register.js exporting register(on, options)), prompt.compose (the docs list prompt.section, prompt.context, prompt.submit), $.tool.call as a method (tool.call is an event; the docs show $.tool.register and $.tool.check), and $.session.root (the docs show $.session with a working-directory accessor). The docs point to typed declarations at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts, which may be older than the installed build.

Gating: mods need CLI v2.1.287+, Desktop v2.1.286+ and VS Code 2.1.299+ for drawing. The docs do not say whether a corporate kill switch or managed policy can turn off mods on a given surface beyond allowManagedModsOnly and disableAllHooks.
No public docs page exists for plugin eval or /skill-doctor in the sources consulted; this survey did not cover them.

capabilities.note: Customize > Skills > '+' > '+ Create skill' > 'Upload a skill', then upload a ZIP whose top level is the skill folder (<name>/SKILL.md). Requires 'Code execution and file creation' (called 'Create and edit files' in the newer layout). Enterprise: Owner must enable both that and 'Skills' under Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy. Team: on by default. Owners can turn off user-created skills. The docs disagree on plans: the Help Center says Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise; claude.com/docs says Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise.

capabilities.capability: Skills: what a skill may contain
capabilities.note: A folder with SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter: name of up to 64 characters that matches the folder name, and description of up to 1,024 characters) plus optional references/, assets/ and scripts/. Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines. Do not put credentials in a skill; a script that needs an outside service should use a connector instead. Follows the Agent Skills spec.

Automatic: Claude sees each skill's name and description and loads SKILL.md when a request matches. Manual: type '/' in the message box and pick the skill, or name it in the request. A skill must be turned on in Customize > Skills.

Skills run in Claude's code sandbox. In chat the whole skill folder, scripts included, is copied into the sandbox; keep script paths relative, such as scripts/x.py. Languages are 'what the code-execution environment provides'; the sandbox article names only 'Python or Javascript'. Network: Free, Pro, Max and Ultra have network on (approved package managers such as PyPI, npm, GitHub, crates.io, Ubuntu and Yarn). Team and Enterprise Owners choose off, package managers only, package managers plus listed domains, or all domains. The same article contradicts itself on the Team default. Enterprise defaults to off. Uploaded files (CSV and others) and project files are readable in the sandbox. Claude can write files the person downloads or saves to Google Drive: .xlsx, .pptx, .docx, PDF, PNG, .csv, .md and .html, up to 30 MB per file.

capabilities.capability: Slash commands / saved prompts by name
capabilities.note: Typing '/' lists your skills, labeled with the plugin each came from, and a plugin's commands appear in the same menu. In chat a plugin command 'loads as a skill; Claude applies it when it fits'; you cannot run it as /plugin:command the way Cowork does. '/' also opens the + menu (connectors). In the new unified experience '/deep-research' starts Research. I found no doc on a separate saved-prompt feature.

All plans; Free is limited to 5 projects. 'Set project instructions' applies to every chat in the project. Project knowledge takes uploaded documents, text and code. On paid plans RAG expands capacity up to 10x. Team and Enterprise can share projects as view or edit. A new beta version of projects is rolling out, starting in Claude Code.

GitHub (all plans, including Free) adds a repository to a chat, or chosen files and folders to a project, with 'Sync now'. Private projects only. It reads file names, file contents and branch content, not commits, PRs or issues. Google Drive adds Docs, Sheets and Slides to a chat or to a private project's knowledge, refreshed periodically; a file over about 10 MB gives only its name and details. The new unified experience lists 'Add from GitHub isn't supported'.

No current Help Center article covers styles: a Help Center search for 'styles' returns none. The personalization article lists only Instructions, Project instructions and Skills, and says to 'use skills when you want to customize how Claude formats and delivers its responses'. Two passing mentions remain: an incognito-chats FAQ mentions 'custom styles', and an undated Academy page names 'Use style' > 'Create & edit styles'.

On by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; on Team and Enterprise, Owners control it. Stored as individual topics, editable in Settings. Each project has its own memory. Memory can be turned off per chat from the + menu. Searching past chats is paid plans only. Memory is shared with Cowork only when Cowork runs in the cloud.

Customize > Connectors > Add > custom, by URL. Free: one custom connector. Pro, Max, Ultra: added to your own account. Team and Enterprise: an Owner adds it under Organization settings > Connectors (on Enterprise, a custom role can too), and members then connect. Authentication choices: OAuth, sign in when needed, or none; request headers are in beta. The server must be reachable over the public internet, because calls come from Anthropic's cloud. The web also renders MCP Apps.

All plans. Artifacts cover documents, code, single-page websites, dashboards and small interactive tools, plus Docs, Slides and Design templates. Requires 'Cloud code execution and file creation'. Artifacts made before September 16, 2026 are 'legacy'.

Store data: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise, in personal or shared storage, up to 100 MB or 25,000 records, plus uploads of up to 20 MB per file and 1 GB in total. Connect apps and custom connectors: Pro and above. 'Artifacts that use Claude': each user signs in and usage counts against their own plan; new artifacts ask permission the first time. The plan table does not list calling Claude.

Plugins exist and include a catalog: Customize > Plugins > Discover (directory on Pro and above), Add marketplace (GitHub or GitHub Enterprise, public GitLab or Bitbucket; up to 25), Upload plugin (.zip or .plugin; up to 200 MB and 5,000 files), and Create with Claude. Paid plans only. In chat: skills load; commands load as skills; a remote http or sse MCP server is listed and works once connected; agents, hooks, local MCP servers, LSP servers, output styles, themes and settings are ignored; a top-level bin/ makes chat refuse the whole plugin. Mods are Claude Code only. Plugins installed on the account sync to Cowork (which loads agents and hooks) and to Claude Code.
Hooks in hooks/hooks.json are 'Ignored' in chat and show grayed out; they load in Cowork and Claude Code.

No doc describes a step that runs after each answer. The only documented automatic interception is Enterprise inference hooks, which run before inference on each prompt and before tool calls run, return allow or deny only, and are configured by the Owner or Primary Owner.
